Eskom Unbundling -- what the future holds

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Eskom, the country's largest power utility is technically insolvent and struggling to keep the lights on. Are we speeding towards Day Zero?

Unique Selling Point:
President Cyril Ramaphosa has announced a decision to unbundle Eskom into three separate state-owned entities, Generation, Transmission and Distribution. The announcement was in all likelihood discussed with the IMF and the World Bank as well as other major investors. But days later, the country was plunged into darkness when the troubled utility announced nationwide Stage 4 load shedding with devastating effect on the country's people and the economy. To sort out Eskom's rot will be a long haul but intervention is urgently needed. Public Enterprises Minister Pravin Gordan has described the crisis as one of the biggest risks to the South African economy. The question we are asking is: How did we get here, how will we fix it? And is unbundling a solution?

Summary:
It will be a long haul to sort out Eskom's rot. Dealing with the financial, operational and structural crises is urgent. It is an emergency says Public Enterprises Minister Pravin Gordin. Lack of maintenance triggered Stage Four loadshedding, plunging the country into darkness with devastating effect on the country's people and the economy. A probe into factors leading to the collapse of the entity is underway.There are those who say that Eskom is a metaphor for South Africa. It's a vast megalith entirely bankrupted by people who have treated it as their personal ATM's and has become a political playing field.This is a disaster threatening to destroy the country's economy. A large part of the rot set in when the government decided to go ahead with building Medupi and Kusile. the world's two largest and most expensive coal-fired plants. Mismanagement and rampant corruption has led to serious delays and an billions of rand overspent. The culture of non-payment and rampant theft of electricity has added to the utilities woes. Municipalities are in arrears of more than R17-Billion. Stage 4 load shedding was implemented . This means that around 40% of generating capacity was not available. Lack of maintenance was one of the contributing factors. Splitting Eskom into three entities has Unions up in arms, already smelling job cuts and privatisation.
The bottom line is,the lights are out for two reasons: Corruption and Mismanagement. On Wednesday Tito Mboweni, Minister of Finance will inform the nation about the way forward.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: President Cyril Ramaphosa has announced a decision to unbundle Eskom into three separate state-owned entities, Generation, Transmission and Distribution. The announcement was in all likelihood discussed with the IMF and the World Bank as well as other major investors. But days later, the country was plunged into darkness when the troubled utility announced nationwide Stage 4 load shedding with devastating effect on the country's people and the economy. To sort out Eskom's rot will be a long haul but intervention is urgently needed. Public Enterprises Minister Pravin Gordan has described the crisis as one of the biggest risks to the South African economy. The question we are asking is: How did we get here, how will we fix it? And is unbundling a solution?
metadata.Summary: It will be a long haul to sort out Eskom's rot. Dealing with the financial, operational and structural crises is urgent. It is an emergency says Public Enterprises Minister Pravin Gordin. Lack of maintenance triggered Stage Four loadshedding, plunging the country into darkness with devastating effect on the country's people and the economy. A probe into factors leading to the collapse of the entity is underway.There are those who say that Eskom is a metaphor for South Africa. It's a vast megalith entirely bankrupted by people who have treated it as their personal ATM's and has become a political playing field.This is a disaster threatening to destroy the country's economy. A large part of the rot set in when the government decided to go ahead with building Medupi and Kusile. the world's two largest and most expensive coal-fired plants. Mismanagement and rampant corruption has led to serious delays and an billions of rand overspent. The culture of non-payment and rampant theft of electricity has added to the utilities woes. Municipalities are in arrears of more than R17-Billion. Stage 4 load shedding was implemented . This means that around 40% of generating capacity was not available. Lack of maintenance was one of the contributing factors. Splitting Eskom into three entities has Unions up in arms, already smelling job cuts and privatisation. The bottom line is,the lights are out for two reasons: Corruption and Mismanagement. On Wednesday Tito Mboweni, Minister of Finance will inform the nation about the way forward.
